mainTopic: Must עדים see and testify together? The סמיכה of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, the הלכה of רבי יהושע בן קרחה, combining loan and admission testimony, and contradictions in בדיקות.
overview: The גמרא gives one more way to explain the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי נתן: everyone agrees the עדים must see the event together, and they argue only about whether they must also testify together. Then comes the story of how רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא received סמיכה from רבי יוחנן, and רבי זירא's lesson that a great man's סמיכה is not taken back. Next the גמרא brings different reports of whether the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה for land and for movable property. Along the way it explains a ברייתא about the signs of adulthood. רב's rule about combining testimony of loans and admissions leads to a back-and-forth between רב נחמן בר יצחק and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, which ends with רב הונא's answer being knocked down. The נהרדעי then say that every combination joins together, following רבי יהושע בן קרחה. Finally, רב יהודה rules that contradictions in the detail questions do not ruin testimony in money cases. רבא limits this to side details, and the גמרא challenges it from רב חסדא's ruling about murder cases.

steps.title: Both sides agree on seeing together, but argue about testifying together
steps.stepSummary: A second explanation: the תנא קמא and רבי נתן both follow the רבנן, and their only argument is whether we compare the testimony to the seeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say that everyone holds like the רבנן who argue with רבי יהושע בן קרחה (so the עדים must see the event together). Their argument here is whether testifying is compared to seeing. One opinion says we compare them, so the עדים must also testify together. The other opinion says we do not compare them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to explain the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי נתן. In this version, neither side follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that the עדים must see the event together. The new question is whether the court testimony (הגדה) has to match the seeing (ראייה). The תנא קמא says yes, so they must also testify together. רבי נתן says no, so they may testify one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees: both sides of the argument hold this
The majority of the Sages, here the ones who argue with רבי יהושע בן קרחה
Comparing two things so that the rules of one apply to the other
The עדים' testimony in court
The עדים' seeing of the event

steps.whatToRemember: In this version, everyone agrees the עדים must see the event together. The only argument is whether they must also testify together, which depends on whether we compare הגדה to ראייה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse the two stages. ראייה means seeing the event, and הגדה means testifying in court. In this explanation, both sides agree about the seeing; they argue only about the testifying.

phrases.english: And everyone holds like the Rabbis
phrases.notes: "Everyone" here means both the תנא קמא and רבי נתן.

phrases.aramaic: דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה,
phrases.english: who disagree with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכָא בְּאַקּוֹשֵׁי הַגָּדָה לִרְאִיָּה קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: and here they disagree about comparing the testimony to the seeing.
phrases.notes: "Testimony" means testifying in court, and "seeing" means witnessing the event.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: we compare the testimony to the seeing,
and the other Sage holds: we do not compare them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּדְכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא כְּרַבָּנַן דִּפְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another way to read the מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי נתן, different from the earlier explanations.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different point: the comparison of הגדה to ראייה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You might have thought the תנא קמא and רבי נתן were really arguing about the opinion of רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both agree with the רבנן that the עדים must see together. They argue only about whether we compare testimony to seeing.

steps.title: Story: trying to ordain רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אליקים had been trying to get סמיכה for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא without success. One day he was sitting before רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אליקים was working hard to get סמיכה for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, but it was not working out. One day he was sitting in front of רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story connected to our topic. This line sets the scene for what comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learn that רבי שמעון בן אליקים wanted his friend to receive סמיכה, but it kept not happening. Sitting before רבי יוחנן gives him the chance he has been waiting for.

keyTerms.meaning: Was working hard at, was eager for
To give him סמיכה (rabbinic ordination)
It did not work out

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים הֲוָה מִשְׁתְּקִיד
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim was striving

phrases.aramaic: עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְמִסְמְכֵיהּ,
phrases.english: to get Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, ordained,
but it was not working out.
One day he was sitting
before Rabbi Yochanan,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים הֲוָה מִשְׁתְּקִיד עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא לְמִסְמְכֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a story that will bring an answer about the opinion of רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: the attempts to give סמיכה to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא had not succeeded, and now he was sitting before רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן asks about the הלכה of רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks his students whether anyone knows if the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to them: Does anyone know whether the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן asks a real question about the הלכה. This question sets up the chance for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא to receive סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה is the תנא who holds that the עדים do not have to see the event together. רבי יוחנן wants to know whether we rule like him.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there anyone who knows?
The final ruling follows (someone's opinion)

phrases.english: He said to them: Is there anyone who knows
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן, speaking to the students sitting before him.

phrases.aramaic: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה, אוֹ לָא?
phrases.english: whether the halakha follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אִיכָּא דְּיָדַע הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה, אוֹ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Inside the story, רבי יוחנן raises the question that opens the door to the סמיכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

steps.title: Ordination first, then the answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אליקים says that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא knows the answer, but asks that רבי יוחנן first give him סמיכה. רבי יוחנן does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אליקים said: This one knows. רבי יוחנן said: Let him say it. He answered: Let the Master first give him סמיכה. So רבי יוחנן gave him סמיכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אליקים uses the moment to finally get his friend ordained. He asks for the סמיכה before the answer is said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer to רבי יוחנן's question is something only רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא knows. רבי שמעון בן אליקים makes the סמיכה come first. His long effort from the start of the story finally succeeds.

keyTerms.meaning: This one knows
First, at the beginning
He gave him סמיכה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים: דֵּין יָדַע.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim said to him: This one knows.
phrases.notes: He is pointing to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

phrases.english: He said to him: Let him say it.
He said to him: Let the Master ordain him first.
He ordained him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי יוחנן's question by pointing to the one who knows, and secures the סמיכה first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן gives סמיכה to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא before hearing the answer.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן קרחה agrees with רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: The newly ordained רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reports what he heard: רבי יהושע בן קרחה agrees with רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: My son, tell me, what did you hear? He said: This is what I heard: רבי יהושע בן קרחה agrees with רבי נתן.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that he has received סמיכה, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gives the information that רבי יוחנן asked for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reports that רבי יהושע בן קרחה agrees with רבי נתן. רבי נתן is the one who holds that the עדים do not have to testify together in בית דין. So רבי יהושע בן קרחה is lenient about seeing together and also about testifying together.

keyTerms.meaning: My son, a warm way a teacher speaks to a student
What did you hear (from your teachers)?
Agrees, concedes

steps.whatToRemember: The report is that רבי יהושע בן קרחה agrees with רבי נתן: the עדים do not need to testify together in בית דין.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: בְּנִי, אֱמוֹר לִי כֵּיצַד שָׁמַעְתָּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: My son, tell me, what did you hear?
He said to him: This is what I heard:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמּוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה לְרַבִּי נָתָן.
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha agrees with Rabbi Natan.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּךְ שָׁמַעְתִּי, שֶׁמּוֹדֶה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה לְרַבִּי נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to רבי יוחנן's question once the סמיכה is done.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע בן קרחה agrees with רבי נתן that the עדים do not have to testify together.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן finds the answer obvious
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן complains that the answer he received was obvious. Someone who does not require the witnesses to see the event together surely does not require them to testify together.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Is this what I needed him for?! Now, if about the main part, the seeing, רבי יהושע בן קרחה said 'we do not need' the witnesses to be together, is it even a question about the telling?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן is disappointed with the answer. He says it was obvious, so he did not really need it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing the event is the main part of עדות, and telling it in בית דין comes second. רבי יהושע בן קרחה already allows the witnesses to see the event separately. So he would surely allow them to testify separately, and the reported tradition adds nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this what I needed? (a complaint that the information was unnecessary)
The main part, which is the seeing of the event
Together, with each other
The telling, meaning the testimony given in בית דין
Is it even a question? (it is obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not saying the answer is wrong. He is saying it is obvious, so he did not need to give סמיכה just to hear it.

phrases.english: He said: Is this what I needed [him] for?!
phrases.notes: The speaker is רבי יוחנן. He means: did I give סמיכה just to hear this?

phrases.english: Now, if regarding the main part, the seeing,

phrases.aramaic: בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha said that together
"we do not need" [it],
is it even a question about the telling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the answer given in step 5 and calls it obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The usefulness of the tradition reported by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a קל וחומר. If the witnesses need not see the event together, which is the main part, then surely they need not testify together, which is the lesser part.

steps.title: The סמיכה is not taken back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא that his סמיכה stays in place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Since you have gone up, you will not come down.
steps.whatsHappening: Even though the answer turned out to be unneeded, רבי יוחנן does not cancel the סמיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סמיכה was given for a reason that turned out to be weak. רבי יוחנן still says it remains in place. Once a person has been raised to this level, he is not brought back down.

keyTerms.meaning: Since you have gone up (received סמיכה)
You will not come down (it is not cancelled)

phrases.english: He said to him: Since you have gone up,
you will not come down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his complaint in step 6, רבי יוחנן still confirms the סמיכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once someone has received סמיכה, it is not taken away, even if the reason for giving it turns out to be unneeded.

steps.title: רבי זירא's lesson: a great person's סמיכה stays
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא learns from the story that once a great person receives סמיכה, it stays.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: Learn from this that a great man, once he has received סמיכה, keeps it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא draws a general rule from the story with רבי יוחנן. This closes the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story turns into a rule. The rule is about a גברא רבה, someone truly worthy. His סמיכה stays even if the reason it was given at that moment did not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this
A great man, a great scholar
He received סמיכה

steps.whatToRemember: When a worthy scholar has received סמיכה, it is not cancelled, even if it was given for a mistaken reason.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: Learn from this,
a great man, once he has received סמיכה,
he stays with סמיכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי יוחנן's words in step 7 into a general rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A great man's סמיכה, once given, stays in place.

steps.title: רב: the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה in all cases
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה for both land and movable items.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה, both for land and for movable items.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from the story to the practical הלכה. רב rules for רבי יהושע בן קרחה in every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This means the witnesses do not have to see the event together. According to רב, that is true whether the case is about land or about movable items.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
Land, real estate
Movable items

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin said that Rav said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha,
both for land and for movable items.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and gives the practical ruling on רבי יהושע בן קרחה's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses do not need to see the event together, both for land and for movable items.

steps.title: עולא: the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה only for land
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules for רבי יהושע בן קרחה only in cases about land, not in cases about movable items.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה for land, but not for movable items.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא disagrees with רב and limits the ruling to cases about land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land cannot move, so two witnesses who saw separately are surely talking about the same field. A movable item might not be the same one each witness saw. So for movable items, עולא does not follow רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

keyTerms.meaning: But not

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a real disagreement between רב and עולא on how far רבי יהושע בן קרחה's leniency goes.

phrases.aramaic: עוּלָּא אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
phrases.english: Ulla said: The halacha follows Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha
for land, but not for movable items.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה בְּקַרְקָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב's ruling in step 9 by leaving out movable items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For land, the witnesses do not need to see the event together. For movable items, they do.

steps.title: אביי asks why עולא said 'הלכה' if there is no argument about land
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges עולא: ruling 'the הלכה follows' implies a dispute, but רב said the חכמים agree with רבי יהושע בן קרחה about land.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to עולא: You said 'the הלכה follows him.' That means you think they argue! But רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא, in the name of רב: the חכמים agree with רבי יהושע בן קרחה about testimony on land!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks עולא's ruling from Step 10. He says that if there is no argument about land, there is no need to 'rule' on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only say 'the הלכה follows X' when someone disagrees with X. עולא ruled like רבי יהושע בן קרחה for land, so he must think the חכמים disagree there. But רב taught that the חכמים agree in land cases, so there is nothing to rule on.

keyTerms.meaning: by implication, it follows that
they disagree
the חכמים agree (admit)
testimony about land

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Ulla):
"The halacha"? That implies that they disagree!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Abba say that Rav Huna said that Rav said:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
phrases.english: The Rabbis agree with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha
in testimony about land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's ruling in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה for land
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'הלכה' ruling assumes a dispute, but רב says there is no dispute about land, since the חכמים agree.

steps.title: A second source: the חכמים agree in several kinds of testimony
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds a ברייתא from רב אידי בר אבין: the חכמים agree with רבי יהושע בן קרחה for a firstborn animal, land, חזקה, and 'the boy and the girl'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אידי בר אבין taught, in the damages laws of the school of קרנא: the חכמים agree with רבי יהושע בן קרחה in testimony about a בכור, about land, about חזקה, and likewise about the boy and the girl.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a second source to back up his challenge. It also says the חכמים agree about land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not a new argument. It makes the קשיא from Step 11 stronger by adding a ברייתא to רב's statement. It also lists more cases where the witnesses do not need to see the event together.

keyTerms.meaning: taught (a ברייתא)
the damages laws taught in the school of קרנא
a firstborn kosher animal
proof of ownership by using the land over time

phrases.english: And Rav Idi bar Avin taught
in the damages laws of the school of Karna:

phrases.aramaic: מוֹדִין חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה
phrases.english: The Rabbis agree with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha
in testimony about a firstborn animal,
and in testimony about land, and in testimony about presumed ownership,
and likewise those of a boy and of a girl.
phrases.notes: This is talking about the hairs that show a child has grown up. The גמרא will soon ask what exactly it means.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא to strengthen אביי's challenge
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים do not disagree about land testimony
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רב אידי בר אבין from the school of קרנא

steps.title: Answer: this is simply one אמורא against another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that עולא holds there is a dispute about land, while רב and רב אידי hold there is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you setting one man against another man? One master (עולא) holds that they disagree, and the other master (רב) holds that they do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers אביי's challenge by saying the sources simply disagree with עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי tried to disprove עולא using רב and the ברייתא. The גמרא says that is not a real problem, because עולא is allowed to read the dispute differently. For עולא the חכמים argue even about land, so a 'הלכה' ruling makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: you are setting one person against another
one master holds

steps.confusionAlert: This does not prove עולא wrong or right. It only says that a different opinion is not a disproof.

phrases.english: Are you setting one man against another man?
One master holds that they disagree,
and the other master holds that they do not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from Steps 11-12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Dispute between אמוראים: the sources do not bind עולא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and the ברייתא should disprove עולא
steps.terutzMaskana: עולא holds there is a dispute about land; רב and רב אידי hold there is not
steps.whatToRemember: עולא: the חכמים argue even about land. רב and רב אידי: they agree about land.

steps.title: What does 'the boy and the girl' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the ברייתא and asks what case 'and likewise those of a boy and a girl' is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and likewise those of a boy and of a girl'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a side question about the ברייתא from Step 12. This line sets up the next step, which tries an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the חכמים agree in the case of 'the boy and the girl', but did not explain it. The גמרא wants to know exactly how the witnesses testify in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: what is
and likewise
those (signs) of a boy and of a girl

phrases.english: What is meant by "and likewise those of a boy and of a girl"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a side question about the ברייתא quoted in Step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What testimony case 'the boy and the girl' refers to

steps.title: First explanation rejected: one hair per witness is half a matter and half a testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests each witness saw one hair in a different place, then rejects this because each testimony is half a matter and half a testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that one witness says he saw one hair on her back and the other says he saw one hair on her belly, that is a problem! This is half a matter and half a testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first explanation of the case and immediately throws it out. This shows that the ברייתא must mean something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two hairs are needed to show a girl has grown up, and two witnesses are needed for testimony. Here each witness saw only one hair (half the matter) and is only one witness (half the testimony). That obviously cannot count, so the ברייתא could not need to teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say
on her back
on her belly
half a matter and half a testimony

phrases.english: If we say: one witness says he saw one hair on her back,
and the other says he saw one on her belly?

phrases.aramaic: הַאי חֲצִי דָבָר וַחֲצִי עֵדוּת הוּא!
phrases.english: This is half a matter and half a testimony!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects an answer to the question in Step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested reading of 'the boy and the girl'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each witness covers only one hair and is only one witness, so the testimony is obviously invalid and needs no teaching

steps.title: Each witness saw two hairs in a different place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its question about 'the boy and the girl': one witness saw two hairs on the back and the other saw two hairs on the abdomen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where one witness says he saw two hairs on her back, and the other says he saw two hairs on her abdomen.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the 'one hair each' idea, the גמרא gives the real case: each witness saw two hairs, just in different spots on the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two hairs are a complete sign of adulthood. So each witness gives a full testimony, not half of one. The only difference between them is where they looked, and that is enough of a difference to need רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule, which the חכמים agree to here.

keyTerms.meaning: Two (hairs), the sign that a child has become an adult
Her back
Her abdomen (belly)

phrases.english: Rather, one says: two on her back,
and one says: two on her abdomen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the case rejected in step 15 with a workable one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the ברייתא means by 'the boy and the girl'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each witness saw a full sign of two hairs, but in different places (back and abdomen).

steps.title: רב יוסף in the name of עולא: the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה for land and movables
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף reports that עולא ruled like רבי יהושע בן קרחה in both land cases and movable-property cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: I say in the name of עולא: the הלכה is like רבי יהושע בן קרחה, both for land and for movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his version of עולא's ruling. Testimonies can be combined like רבי יהושע בן קרחה says, in every kind of money case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10, עולא was quoted as ruling like רבי יהושע בן קרחה for land but explicitly not for movables. רב יוסף has a different tradition: עולא ruled like him for movable property too. This sets up a competing report about רב in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Land, real estate
Movable property (money, objects)
In the name of

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I say in the name of Ulla:
the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa,
both with regard to land and with regard to movable property.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אֲנָא אָמֵינָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the question of what the הלכה is, after finishing the explanation of the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to עולא, testimonies combine like רבי יהושע בן קרחה for both land and movables.

steps.title: The רבנן of מחוזא in the name of רב: land only, not movables
steps.stepSummary: A different tradition, from רבי זירא in the name of רב, limits רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule to land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן who came from מחוזא say: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: for land, yes, but not for movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report gives a narrower ruling. רב follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה only in land cases, not in cases of movable property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This flips the earlier reports. In step 9 רב ruled for everything, and in step 10 עולא ruled for land only. Now עולא (as רב יוסף reports him) applies the rule to everything, while רב (as רבי זירא reports him) applies it only to land.

keyTerms.meaning: The scholars who came from מחוזא (a town in בבל)
Yes

phrases.english: But the Sages who came from Meḥoza say:
Rabbi Zeira says in the name of Rav:
With regard to land, yes,
phrases.notes: He means: for land, the הלכה follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה.

phrases.english: but not with regard to movable property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing, narrower tradition next to step 17's broad ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב, testimonies combine like רבי יהושע בן קרחה for land only, not for movables.

steps.title: רב is consistent: when admissions and loans combine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב's narrow view fits his own rule: admission after admission, or admission after loan, combine. Loan after loan, or loan after admission, do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב follows his own reasoning, because רב said: an admission after an admission, or an admission after a loan, combine. A loan after a loan, or a loan after an admission, do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the report about רב by quoting another rule of his. In that rule he also refuses to combine two witnesses when they saw two separate money events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An admission ('I owe him') speaks about a debt that already exists, so it can refer to the same debt another witness saw or heard about. Two loans are two separate events. And a loan that comes after an admission cannot be the debt that was admitted earlier. So in movable-money cases רב does not combine separate events, which matches his ruling in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: רב follows his own consistent reasoning
An admission (the borrower says in front of a witness that he owes money)
A loan (the witness saw the money being lent)
They combine (into one full testimony of two witnesses)

steps.whatToRemember: Admission + admission, or loan then admission: the two witnesses combine. Loan + loan, or admission then loan: they do not combine, because they describe separate events.
steps.confusionAlert: The order matters. 'Admission after loan' combines, but 'loan after admission' does not. Read 'אַחַר' carefully: the second word in each pair is the event that happened first.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for joining two single witnesses in a loan claim, and it explains why רב limits רבי יהושע בן קרחה's rule.

phrases.english: Rav follows his own reasoning, as Rav says:
An admission following an admission,
an admission following a loan, combine.
phrases.notes: One witness saw the loan, and later the other heard the borrower admit it. Both can be talking about the same debt.

phrases.english: A loan following a loan,
a loan following an admission, do not combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 18's report about רב by showing it fits another known ruling of his.
steps.raayaObject: The tradition that רב does not follow רבי יהושע בן קרחה for movable property.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's own rule about combining testimonies of admissions and loans.

steps.title: Why should admissions combine if loans don't?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע why admission after admission should combine. The reason loans don't combine is that each witness may have seen a different מנה, and the same doubt seems to apply to admissions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק met רב הונא son of רב יהושע. He said to him: Why is a loan after a loan different, so that the witnesses don't combine? Because the מנה this witness saw, that witness did not see. But with an admission after an admission too, maybe the מנה he admitted in front of this witness is not the one he admitted in front of that witness?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רב's rule from Step 19. He says the reason given for loans should apply equally to admissions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two loans can't combine because each witness may have seen a different loan, so each one testifies about a different debt. רב נחמן בר יצחק argues that two admissions have the same problem: the borrower may have admitted two different debts. So why should admissions combine?

keyTerms.meaning: He met him / found him
What is different?
A loan after a loan (each witness saw a separate loan)
An admission after an admission (each witness heard a separate admission)
A sum of one hundred זוז

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak met
Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua.
He said to him: What is different about
a loan after a loan, that it does not combine?
Because the מנה that this witness saw,
that witness did not see.
An admission after an admission also:
the מנה he admitted in front of this witness,
phrases.notes: Read it as "maybe": perhaps he was admitting a different debt each time.

phrases.english: he did not admit in front of that witness?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי שְׁנָא הַלְוָאָה אַחַר הַלְוָאָה דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction רב drew in Step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that admission after admission combines.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason loans don't combine is that the witnesses may have seen two different debts. That same doubt exists with two admissions, so they shouldn't combine either.

steps.title: The borrower told the second witness it was the same מנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the case is where the borrower told the second witness that the מנה he was admitting is the same one he admitted before the first witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he said to this second witness: The מנה I admitted in front of you, I also admitted in front of so-and-so.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers by narrowing the case. The borrower himself linked the two admissions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the borrower tells the second witness that this is the same debt he admitted before, the two testimonies are about one מנה. A loan can't be linked this way, because two acts of lending are two separate events.

keyTerms.meaning: The last / second one (here, the second witness)
I admitted
In front of you
So-and-so

phrases.english: Where he said to this last witness:
phrases.notes: "He" is the borrower, the one admitting the debt.

phrases.english: This מנה that I admitted to him in front of you,
I also admitted it to him in front of so-and-so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20 by defining the case narrowly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (the borrower linked the admissions).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two admissions might be about two different debts, just like two loans.
steps.terutzMaskana: In רב's case, the borrower told the second witness it was the same מנה, so the testimonies are about one debt.

steps.title: But the first witness still doesn't know
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back: only the second witness knows it is the same debt. The first witness doesn't, so the testimonies still don't fully match.
steps.simpleTranslation: Still, the last witness knows, but the first witness does not know.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges the answer from Step 21. Only one of the two witnesses knows the two admissions are linked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the testimonies to combine, both witnesses should be talking about the same debt. The first witness heard only a plain admission and has no idea it connects to a later one. So the link is known to only one witness.

keyTerms.meaning: Still / even so
The first one (here, the first witness)
Knows

phrases.english: Still, the last witness knows,
the first witness does not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַכַּתִּי, בָּתְרָא יָדַע, קַמָּא לָא יָדַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's answer that the borrower told the second witness.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Linking the debts is only known to one witness, so the first witness's testimony is still not clearly about the same מנה.

steps.title: The borrower went back and told the first witness too
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the borrower went back and told the first witness that the same מנה was also admitted before the second witness. Now both witnesses know it is one debt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he went back and said to the first witness: This מנה that I admitted in front of you, I also admitted in front of so-and-so.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers again by narrowing the case further. The borrower told both witnesses about the link.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now each witness knows his admission is the same debt the other heard. So both are clearly testifying about one מנה, and their testimony can combine.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back / returned
Goes

phrases.english: Where he went back and said to the first witness:
This מנה that I admitted to him in front of you,
I also admitted it to him in front of so-and-so.
phrases.notes: This time "so-and-so" is the second witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the second witness knew the admissions were linked.
steps.terutzMaskana: The borrower told the first witness as well, so both know it is one debt.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק accepts the answer
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק is satisfied and blesses רב הונא for settling his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: May your mind be at rest, because you have put my mind at rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק accepts the answer and thanks רב הונא with a blessing. The next step shows that רב הונא himself does not think the answer holds up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For now the question seems resolved: admissions combine because the borrower linked them for both witnesses, while separate loans can't be linked that way. In step 25, רב הונא reveals that רבא already attacked this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: May your mind be at rest (a blessing)
You have put my mind at rest

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע's explanation: the two admissions combine when the borrower told each witness that it was the same מנה. But the next step reports that רבא (or רב ששת) knocked this explanation down.

phrases.english: He said to him: May your mind be at rest,
for you have put my mind at rest.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: תָּנוּחַ דַּעְתְּךָ שֶׁהִתְנַחְתָּ אֶת דַּעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the answer of Step 23 and closes the exchange.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב נחמן בר יצחק accepts רב הונא's answer that the borrower linked the admissions for both witnesses. Step 25 then reports that this answer was knocked down.

steps.title: רב הונא reveals his answer was already knocked down
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tells רב נחמן בר יצחק not to feel settled, because רבא (or רב ששת) attacked the answer: once the borrower links the two admissions, the case is really the same as הודאה אחר הלוואה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is there to be settled about? רבא, and some say רב ששת, threw an ax at it. Isn't this just the same as an admission after a loan?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא, who gave the answer, now says it does not really hold up, because רבא (or רב ששת) already attacked it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the borrower told each witness that it was the same מנה. רבא's attack is that with this explanation, 'admission after admission' is no different from 'admission after loan,' so it adds nothing new. The answer that made רב נחמן בר יצחק happy now seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: Settling of the mind, feeling satisfied
Threw an ax at it, meaning he attacked and knocked down the idea
An admission after a loan: one witness saw the loan, the other heard the borrower admit it
And some say (a different name for who said it)

steps.confusionAlert: The one attacking the answer here is the same רב הונא who gave it. He is not changing sides. He is telling his friend that רבא already broke it.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is settling?
phrases.notes: רב הונא is answering רב נחמן בר יצחק's blessing from the step before.

phrases.english: For Rava, and some say Rav Sheshet,
threw an ax at it —
phrases.notes: A picture phrase: he chopped the answer down.

phrases.english: isn't this the same as an admission after a loan?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי נִיחוּתָא? דְּרָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, שְׁדָא בַּהּ נַרְגָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Undercuts the satisfaction expressed in step 24 by reporting an outside attack on the answer from steps 21 and 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's explanation that the borrower linked both admissions to one מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the borrower ties the admissions together, the case adds nothing beyond הודאה אחר הלוואה, so the separate ruling about הודאה אחר הודאה becomes pointless.

steps.title: Building palm trees and knocking them down
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק remarks that this is what he heard about them: they knock down palm trees and stand them up again. They build a fine answer and then destroy it themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what I heard about you: you knock down palm trees and stand them up.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק reacts with a saying. The answer he liked has been taken apart by its own side, and this line of reasoning ends here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument is added. The saying confirms that the explanation from steps 21-23 does not survive. The גמרא then brings the broader view of the נהרדעי in step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: That you knock down
Palm trees
And you stand up (again)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַיְינוּ דִּשְׁמִיעַ לִי עֲלַיְיכוּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what I heard about you,
phrases.notes: "You" is plural. He means רב הונא and his group of חכמים.

phrases.english: that you knock down palm trees and stand them up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 25, accepting that the explanation has collapsed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא's answer about the borrower linking the two admissions is knocked down, so this approach ends.

steps.title: נהרדעי: all combinations of testimony join together
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of נהרדעא rule that admission after admission, admission after loan, loan after loan, and loan after admission all combine into one testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נהרדעי say: whether it is an admission after an admission, an admission after a loan, a loan after a loan, or a loan after an admission, they combine.
steps.whatsHappening: A different group of חכמים, the נהרדעי, gives a wider view than רב's: every kind of pairing of witnesses joins together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the question was which pairs combine, and the case of loan after loan did not. The נהרדעי do not split the cases at all. Even two witnesses who each saw a different loan event combine, as long as both testify about the same amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים of the city of נהרדעא
A loan after a loan: each witness saw a separate lending event
They combine into one full testimony

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling removes the worry that each witness may have seen a different מנה, which drove the whole back-and-forth in steps 20-25.

phrases.english: The Nehardeans say:
whether an admission after an admission,
or an admission after a loan,
or a loan after a loan,
or a loan after an admission —
they combine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 26 drops רב הונא's approach, this gives a different, all-inclusive view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All four pairings of loan and admission testimony combine into one testimony.

steps.title: Whose view is this? רבי יהושע בן קרחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose opinion the נהרדעי follow and answers: רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like whom? Like רבי יהושע בן קרחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the נהרדעי's wide ruling to the earlier תנא who holds this way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן קרחה holds that if both witnesses testify about the same sum, it counts as one testimony, even if they saw different events. That is exactly why the נהרדעי can let every combination join.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
The תנא who holds that testimonies about the same sum combine

steps.whatToRemember: The נהרדעי say all pairings of loan and admission combine, and the גמרא explains that their view follows רבי יהושע בן קרחה. This is broader than רב's rule in step 19.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korcha.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the תנא behind the ruling in step 27.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the נהרדעי are following
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהושע בן קרחה, who counts testimonies about the same sum as one testimony

steps.title: Contradiction in detail questions is fine in money cases
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that if witnesses contradict each other in the בדיקות (the detail questions), their testimony is still valid in דיני ממונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Testimony that contradicts itself, one witness against the other, in the בדיקות is valid in money cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: what happens when two witnesses disagree on side details of their story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בדיקות are the judges' detail questions, not the main facts. רב יהודה says that in money cases a clash on these details does not throw out the testimony. Saying "in money cases" suggests that in capital cases it would be different.

keyTerms.meaning: Testimony that contradicts, where the witnesses' stories clash
One against the other (the two witnesses' accounts)
Detail questions the judges ask about side facts
Money cases

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying contradictions never matter. It is only about בדיקות, the side details, and only in money cases.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
testimony that contradicts, one against the other,
in the examinations,
is valid in monetary cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: עֵדוּת הַמַּכְחֶשֶׁת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ בִּבְדִיקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the combining discussion ends in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who contradict each other in the בדיקות remain valid in דיני ממונות.

steps.title: רבא limits רב יהודה's ruling to side details
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב יהודה's ruling makes sense when the witnesses disagree about a side detail, such as the color of the purse. But if they disagree about the money itself, such as the color of the coins, their testimonies do not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: רב יהודה's statement makes sense when one witness says the money was in a black purse and the other says it was in a white purse. But if one says it was a black מנה and the other says it was a white מנה, their testimonies do not combine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is setting a limit on רב יהודה's rule from the last step. Only small side details can be contradicted without ruining the testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purse is only a container, so a witness could easily forget its color. The coins are the actual loan the witnesses came to testify about. A contradiction about them suggests that one of the witnesses is lying.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it is reasonable
Purse or money bag
A sum of money (100 זוז); here, the coins of the loan
Combine (the two testimonies join together into one valid testimony)

phrases.english: Rava says:
The statement of Rav Yehuda is reasonable
where one says: "In a black purse,"
and one says: "In a white purse."
But if one says: "A black maneh,"
phrases.notes: "Black" here means the coins looked dark, as opposed to shiny white ones.

phrases.english: and one says: "A white maneh,"
their testimonies do not combine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רב יהודה's ruling from step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A contradiction about a side detail (the purse) does not ruin monetary testimony. A contradiction about the money itself (the coins) does.

steps.title: Challenge from רב חסדא: clothing color doesn't matter even in murder cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does a contradiction about a side detail, like the color of the purse, really ruin testimony in דיני נפשות? רב חסדא rules that in a murder case, disagreeing about the weapon ruins the testimony, but disagreeing about the color of the killer's clothes does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in capital cases, would a black purse not be accepted? But didn't רב חסדא say: if one witness says "he killed him with a sword" and the other says "he killed him with an ariran," this is not "established." If one says "his clothes were black" and the other says "his clothes were white," this is "established."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges what follows from רב יהודה's rule. He limited it to דיני ממונות, which suggests that in capital cases even a side-detail contradiction ruins the testimony. רב חסדא says otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said contradictions in the detail questions are fine "in money cases." That suggests they are not fine in capital cases. But רב חסדא shows that even in a murder case, a contradiction about a side detail like clothing color does not ruin the testimony. Only a contradiction about something central, like the weapon, does.

keyTerms.meaning: Capital cases (cases of life and death)
Sword
A different kind of weapon
Established, consistent: testimony that holds together
His garments

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not against the money-case ruling itself. It targets what that ruling implies: that capital cases would be stricter about side details.

phrases.english: And a black purse in capital cases, not?
But doesn't Rav Chisda say:
one says: "He killed him with a sword,"
and one says: "He killed him with an ariran,"
this is not "established";
phrases.notes: "נכון" comes from the פסוק "וְהִנֵּה אֱמֶת נָכוֹן הַדָּבָר" (דברים יג:טו): testimony that holds up.

phrases.english: one says: "His garments were black,"
and one says: "His garments were white,"
this is "established."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַרְנָקִי שְׁחוֹרָה בְּדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת לָא? וְהָאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the implication of רב יהודה's ruling (as explained by רבא) that side-detail contradictions would ruin testimony in capital cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication of רב יהודה's rule that in דיני נפשות, contradictions in side details invalidate testimony.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא rules that in a murder case, contradicting each other about the killer's clothing color still leaves the testimony "נכון." So side details do not ruin testimony even in capital cases.
